title: Coherence of normalized etale sum right adjoints
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. All schemes below are Noetherian (admit finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings), and all arrows are separated and finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Give the arrows and their composites compactifications [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write $F_a=Ra_!\dashv G_a$ with counit $\varepsilon_a$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. For etale $a$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], put $S_a=D(a_{\Sigma!})\dashv a^*$ with counit $\operatorname{ev}_a$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension, lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], take $d_a:F_a\xrightarrow{\sim}S_a$ from the proper-support/sum identification [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact], and define $\rho_a=(d_a^{-1})^c:G_a\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*$ and $\eta_a=\rho_{a,A}$ followed by the pullback-unit identification [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate].

For composable etale $e:U\to X$ and $v:X\to T$, let $c_{v,e}:G_{ve}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_eG_v$ be the adjunction conjugate of the specified compact-support compositor, using the composite adjunction [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. For every $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$,
$$\rho_{ve,K}=e^*(\rho_{v,K})\circ\rho_{e,G_vK}\circ c_{v,e,K},$$
with the pullback-composition comparison inserted. For an identity arrow this is the canonical identity comparison.

For a Cartesian base change of an etale $e:U\to X$ along any $w:X'\to X$, write $e':U'\to X'$, $w':U'\to U$ for the pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let $C_{e,w}:w^*F_e\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{e'}w'^*$ be the specified compactification exchange [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Define $b_{e,w}:w'^*G_eA_X\to G_{e'}A_{X'}$ as the $F_{e'}\dashv G_{e'}$ adjunct of $w^*\varepsilon_{e,A_X}\circ C_{e,w,G_eA_X}^{-1}$ followed by $w^*A_X\cong A_{X'}$. Then
$$\eta_{e'}\circ b_{e,w}=w'^*\eta_e.$$
The normalizations include the following equality of derived evaluation counits. If $b^\Sigma:w^*S_e\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{e'}w'^*$ is the inverse of the degreewise sum-extension comparison [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map, lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], then, after the pullback identifications,
$$w^*\operatorname{ev}_{e,A_X}\circ(b^\Sigma_{e^*A_X})^{-1}=\operatorname{ev}_{e',A_{X'}}.$$
These identities use the actual compositor and exchange, agree under proper refinement, and are compatible with further Cartesian open restriction.

proof.text: Use the identity and cocycle clauses of unboundedEtaleCompactSupport_comparison_coherence to identify the inverse pairwise compactification comparison with its reverse. The chosen self comparison is the identity, so etaleSumSupportIso is the canonical graph comparison. The normalized fixed-compactification compositor is therefore the specified chosen compositor. Apply etaleNormalizedMates_composition and etaleNormalizedMates_identity. For refinement precompose the normalized refinement equation with the inverse conjugate and cancel.

source.place: Tags 0F7J and 0F7K; fixed-compactification normalization and comparison cocycle

proof.text: Prove compatibility of etaleSumPullbackUnitIso with the exact pullback compositor. Transport leftDerivedUpperStarComp_hom_app_unit through leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory, rewriting its oplax unit by leftDerivedUpperStarUnitIso_hom_eq_η and using naturality. Express the exact square comparison as the inverse of one compositor followed by the other; the two unit-composition equations then prove its coefficient-unit square.

For an arbitrary Cartesian square, first use EtaleSupportExchange.rightMate_eq for the canonical pullback square. The normalized support exchange for the pulled-back compactification equals exchangeIso, since its final self-comparison is the identity. Factor the arbitrary square through its canonical pullback isomorphism, over the identity of the new base. Apply etaleNormalizedMates_openRestriction to that identity-base square and etaleNormalizedMates_normalization_pasting to these two squares. Rewrite the pullback-isomorphism projection equations. This yields the full normalized right-mate equation for the original square and arbitrary target compactification.

source.place: Step 1; right-mate normalization and Cartesian pasting

proof.text: The chosen compact-support exchange equals the fixed-compactification normalized exchange by unboundedEtaleCompactSupport_baseChange and the chosen self-comparison identity. Hence their inverses agree. The exchange-adjunct clause of etaleNormalizedMates and naturality of the adjunction hom bijection identify the defined coefficient b with B at the coefficient object followed by the right adjoint applied to the coefficient pullback unit. Apply naturality of rho, the preceding full right-mate equation, and the coefficient-unit square. This is exactly b followed by eta prime equals the pullback of eta followed by the coefficient-unit identification.

source.place: Step 1; coefficient specialization of the right-mate equation

proof.text: Specialize the derived evaluation equation of etaleSumExchangeCounit to constantComplex. The flipped inverse-image square is the inverse of the original one. Use the coefficient-unit square to express its component followed by the pullback of the base coefficient unit as the displayed three-factor coefficient comparison. Naturality of the derived evaluation counit and functoriality give the required evaluation equality.

source.place: Tag 03S6; derived evaluation and coefficient specialization

proof.text: For further Cartesian open restriction, postcompose both sides with the invertible eta for the final etale arrow. Apply the base-change normalization already proved to each of the three squares. Naturality of the exact pullback compositor moves the original eta across it. The coefficient-unit composition equation identifies the remaining factors. Cancel the final eta. This proves pasting of the actual defined b maps without a new normalization.
